:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width='60%'}
::: {style='font-size: 75%'}
1. Modify the code to account for the presence of the `Trial` class
    - *Don't forget to add the run number to your Logger class!*
1. Generate an animation for each run of the model. Do they differ significantly?
1. Explore some of the EventLogger and TrialLogger visualisations
    - Recreate `plot_metric()` from the slides, but for a queue not shown there - try the specialist wait (`specialist_wait_begins` → `being_seen_by_specialist`)
    - Try `plot_resource_utilisation()`, which wasn't covered on the slides, to compare utilisation across your three resource types
1. Create and display both a static and an interactive process map of this system
    - *You can build these step by step, or use the `generate_dfg()` shortcut on the `TrialLogger`*
:::
:::

::: {.column width='40%'}
::: {.fragment}
::: {style='font-size: 60%; color: lightgrey'}
### Extensions
- Play around with some of the parameters available for the static process maps: [LINK](https://hsma-tools.github.io/vidigi/reference/process_mapping.dfg_to_graphviz.html)
- Try out the parameters available for the interactive version of the process maps: [LINK](https://hsma-tools.github.io/vidigi/reference/process_mapping.dfg_to_cytoscape.html)
- Try exploring some of the comparison plots: [`plot_scenario_comparison`](https://hsma-tools.github.io/vidigi/reference/plots.plot_scenario_comparison.html), [`plot_resource_utilisation_comparison`](https://hsma-tools.github.io/vidigi/reference/plots.plot_resource_utilisation_comparison.html) and `plot_event_duration_comparison`. You'll need a second trial run under different parameters to compare against. What do you need to pass to these to run these commands? [**HINT: the first two are plain functions - import them from the `plots` module and pass each trial's combined event log. `plot_event_duration_comparison` has no standalone equivalent - it's a `TrialLogger` method, so call it directly and pass it the other `TrialLogger` to compare against.**]{style="color:lightgrey"}
- Try modifying one of the plots you created from the TrialLogger class to polish it by applying a new theme or some other tweaks. You might want to take a look at the plotly theming documentation: [LINK](https://plotly.com/python/templates/) for some ideas.
:::
